description.content:
Open an embedded checkout session and get the URL to send the person to.

The files are fetched when the session is opened (signed links may expire
a few minutes later) and their pages counted. The URL takes at most one
order and stops working after 24 hours. Test keys open test sessions:
the order is a sandbox order and no account is opened. Live sessions need
a key with embedded checkout enabled.

Whether Expedited Plus can be ordered right now.

Worth calling before placing the order: it is gated on Eastern business
hours and on the language pair, so a caller can fall back to ordinary
expedited instead of having the order rejected.

Delivery estimates for a page count, on each service level.

Served from here so an integration quotes what the website quotes. The
same promise computed in two places drifts, and the customer is the one
who finds out.

The languages that can be used as languageFrom or languageTo.

Served from the same list the order form renders, so an integrator cannot
build against a code the site does not accept.

Place an order with its source documents attached.

Send `Idempotency-Key` and a retried request returns the original order
rather than a second one. Without it, a network timeout on the client's
side turns into two orders and two invoices.

Register where to be told that an order moved.

The signing secret comes back once. Every delivery carries
`X-Everbary-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 over
"<t>.<raw body>" with that secret - verify it before trusting the payload,
and reject a timestamp more than a few minutes old.

info.description: Place and track certified translation orders (USCIS, courts, universities). Set the collection variable apiKey to a test key (ev_test_...) to use the sandbox. Docs: https://orders.everbary.com/v1/docs · https://www.everbary.com/integrations/api
